podcast.title: "Camp Demeanor" and The Kinks Name
podcast.body: Pete Quayfe's "camp demeanor" was one of the factors Larry Page considered when proposing "The Kinks" as the group's name. Page believed this aspect, along with Dave Davis's, would contribute to the controversial and attention-grabbing nature of the name. "especially given the camp demeanor of both Dave Davis and Pete Quave, it would make sense to call the group The Kinks."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Early Guitar Playing - Hank Marvin Imitation
podcast.body: Pete Quayfe was an early guitar companion of Ray Davis, with Quayfe being able to perform a "possible imitation of Hank Marvin playing a patchy," demonstrating his early guitar skills. "when they first played guitar together at school, while Quayf could do a possible imitation of Hank Marvin playing a patchy."

podcast.title: Hornsey Art School Dropout
podcast.body: Pete Quayfe enrolled in Hornsey Art School after leaving regular school but "dropped out of art school relatively soon after enrolling." He was "kicked out for Teddyboy behaviour," but his primary reason for leaving was his discomfort as a "working class lad, mixing with Bohemian middle-class people." "Quayf also dropped out of art school relatively soon after enrolling. He was kicked out for Teddyboy behaviour, but his main problem was that he didn't feel comfortable as a working class lad, mixing with Bohemian middle-class people."
